transcript.text: Could you turn the attached article.txt about tiny urban forests into a podcast chat between two hosts, explaining what tiny urban forests are and discussing the article’s main points without making up any facts? I like the idea of hearing the topic talked through, because that feels a little more approachable to me than reading it on the page. What I have in mind is a friendly, curious back-and-forth rather than anything newsreader-ish, with two clearly different English voices, one male and one female, and a running time of roughly 90 seconds. I’m a little worried about it sounding stiff instead of like a conversation. Please don’t include any music, and give me the finished audio rather than just a script.

Your tiny-forests chat is about three-quarters done. The account ran out of credits before I could make the last part, so here is what I have so far.

**Download (75 seconds, no music):** http://127.0.0.1:8000/films/43402c182a6a402a8298d12a4a9f1399.mp4

- **It's a video file, not an audio-only file.** These tools have no plain speech-to-audio option. The only way to get two different voices was a video model that makes speech along with the picture. So the file shows two hosts in a small studio: Maya (female, British English) and Tom (male). You can play it just to listen, or turn it into an MP3 with any free converter.
- **The ending is missing.** I made 5 of the 6 planned 15-second parts, so it runs about 75 seconds instead of 90. The missing part was Tom: "So, the takeaway?" / Maya: "Urban ecologists agree on one thing: a tiny forest is not a substitute for protecting existing large trees." / Tom: "Because the big trees store far more carbon. Good to know!" The account needs about 360 more credits for it. Once you have them, I can make it and add it to the end.
- **I haven't been able to listen to it.** The model generates the speech itself, so please check these things:
  - that it follows the script word for word
  - that the voices stay the same from one part to the next
  - that it doesn't read the speaker names ("Maya:", "Tom:") out loud

**What the file covers:** every line comes from your article, with no added facts:
- what tiny forests are: lots about the size of a tennis court, in cities across Europe and Asia
- Akira Miyawaki's method: 3–5 native saplings per square metre in enriched soil, competing for light
- that they can be self-sustaining in about three years
- the benefits: cooler streets, more insects and birds, a place for schoolchildren to learn
- the criticism: thin evidence, and many saplings dying

The hosts also react to each other ("Like, bonsai?", "Is there a catch?") to keep it chatty rather than newsreader-like.
